_source.w: We are learning to analyse modifications to equipment, rules, and scoring that support fair play and inclusive participation.
y: Fair play and inclusion are fundamental values in sport and physical activity.
Analysing modifications develops our understanding of equity versus equality.
These analytical skills help us advocate for inclusive practices in all contexts.
eg: Analysing how a rule modification changes the fairness of a game.
Evaluating equipment modifications used in para-sports and adaptive activities.
Discussing how scoring systems can be designed to reward effort and improvement, not just winning.
Investigating how different sports organisations promote inclusive participation.
Proposing and evaluating a modification to make a class activity more inclusive.
Comparing the inclusiveness of two different versions of the same game.

toLevel2.question: What are modifications in physical activity?
toLevel2.correct: Changes to equipment, rules, or scoring to support fair play and inclusion

distractors.answer: Strict enforcement of the standard rules so that every game is played identically each time
distractors.explanation: Modifications adjust play for inclusion; they are not strict standardisation.

distractors.answer: Changes made only to the uniforms and team colours rather than to how the game runs
distractors.explanation: Modifications change equipment, rules or scoring, not just appearance.

distractors.answer: Adjustments that make a game harder so that only the strongest players can take part
distractors.explanation: Modifications widen access rather than narrowing it to the strongest.

toLevel2.question: What are examples of modified equipment?
toLevel2.correct: Lighter balls, smaller bats, larger goals, or softer surfaces for safety

distractors.answer: Heavier balls, longer bats, and smaller goals to make the game much more difficult
distractors.explanation: Modified equipment is usually easier and safer, not harder.

distractors.answer: Brighter uniforms and team logos that change the look but not the play of a game
distractors.explanation: Equipment modifications change how the game is played, not just its look.

distractors.answer: Official competition gear kept exactly to standard size so that nothing is ever altered
distractors.explanation: Modified equipment is deliberately changed, not kept to standard.

toLevel2.question: What can rule modifications do?
toLevel2.correct: Change how a game is played to suit different players' skills and needs

distractors.answer: Change only the final score at the end without altering how the game is played
distractors.explanation: Rule modifications change play itself, not only the final score.

distractors.answer: Make the game far more difficult so that fewer players are able to keep up
distractors.explanation: Rule modifications widen participation rather than reducing it.

distractors.answer: Keep every rule exactly the same for all players regardless of their needs
distractors.explanation: Rule modifications adjust the rules to suit different needs.

toLevel2.question: What can scoring modifications do?
toLevel2.correct: Change how points are earned so games stay fair across different players

distractors.answer: Change the equipment used while leaving the way that points are earned untouched
distractors.explanation: Scoring modifications change how points are earned, not the equipment.

distractors.answer: Remove scoring entirely so that no game ever has a winner or a loser
distractors.explanation: Scoring is adjusted to stay fair, not removed altogether.

distractors.answer: Make points harder to earn so that only the most skilled players can ever score
distractors.explanation: Scoring modifications keep play fair, not harder for most players.

toLevel2.question: What does inclusive participation mean?
toLevel2.correct: Everyone has a fair chance to take part regardless of ability or background
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Inclusion means a fair chance for all.

distractors.answer: Only the most talented players are selected so that the team can perform at its best
distractors.explanation: Inclusion gives everyone a fair chance, not only the talented.

distractors.answer: Players take part strictly according to their age and never their ability level
distractors.explanation: Inclusion is about fair access for all, not age-only grouping.

distractors.answer: Everyone watches the same game but only a chosen few are allowed to play it
distractors.explanation: Inclusion means taking part, not just watching.

toLevel2.question: What is adapted sport?
toLevel2.correct: Sport with modified equipment, rules, or scoring to suit a wider range of players

distractors.answer: Sport played strictly to official rules with no changes allowed for any participant
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport uses modifications, unlike strict standard play.

distractors.answer: Sport that has been made deliberately harder to challenge only elite competitors
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport widens access rather than narrowing it to elites.

distractors.answer: Sport in which only the uniforms and the venues change while the rules stay fixed
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport changes equipment, rules or scoring, not just venues.

toLevel2.question: What are mixed-ability teams?
toLevel2.correct: Teams where players of different abilities play alongside one another

distractors.answer: Teams formed only from players who share exactly the same level of ability
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability teams combine different abilities, not identical ones.

distractors.answer: Teams that are graded so the strongest players never mix with the weakest
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability teams deliberately mix abilities together.

distractors.answer: Teams chosen purely by age, keeping all ability levels strictly separated
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability teams mix abilities rather than separating them.

toLevel2.question: Why are modified games used in school PE?
toLevel2.correct: They support all learners by adjusting equipment, rules, or scoring
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Modified games used in school PE.

distractors.answer: They identify the strongest students so that the rest can be left out of play
distractors.explanation: Modified games include all learners, not exclude most of them.

distractors.answer: They keep the rules fixed so that every lesson runs in precisely the same way
distractors.explanation: Modified games adjust rules; they do not keep them fixed.

distractors.answer: They make games tougher so that only confident students choose to join in
distractors.explanation: Modified games widen participation rather than discouraging it.

toLevel2.question: What is Paralympic sport?
toLevel2.correct: International sport for athletes with disabilities, with adapted rules and equipment

distractors.answer: International sport that is open only to athletes without any disability at all
distractors.explanation: Paralympic sport is for athletes with disabilities.

distractors.answer: Local school sport that uses exactly the same rules as able-bodied competition
distractors.explanation: Paralympic sport is international and uses adapted rules.

distractors.answer: Sport in which the rules are made deliberately harder for athletes with disabilities
distractors.explanation: Paralympic rules are adapted to enable competition, not made harder.

toLevel2.question: How can Auslan support deaf athletes?
toLevel2.correct: Auslan signed instructions and signals support deaf athletes' full participation

distractors.answer: Auslan replaces the playing rules so that deaf athletes follow a different game
distractors.explanation: Auslan supports communication; it does not change the game's rules.

distractors.answer: Auslan is used only off the field and never during the actual game play
distractors.explanation: Auslan signals support participation during play.

distractors.answer: Auslan signals are useful for coaches but give players nothing to act on
distractors.explanation: Auslan signals support the deaf athletes' own participation.

toLevel2.question: Why are bench rotations used in inclusive games?
toLevel2.correct: Rotating who plays makes sure all players get game time, not just the strongest

distractors.answer: Rotating who plays guarantees that the strongest players are always kept on the field
distractors.explanation: Rotation shares game time rather than favouring the strongest.

distractors.answer: Rotating who plays mainly speeds up the game rather than sharing out game time
distractors.explanation: Rotation is about fair game time, not pace.

distractors.answer: Rotating who plays is used only when a team is already far ahead on points
distractors.explanation: Rotation supports inclusion throughout, not only when ahead.

toLevel2.question: How can goal handicaps even up scoring?
toLevel2.correct: A stronger team may score from further away or with extra rules to balance the game

distractors.answer: A stronger team is simply given more points at the start before the game even begins
distractors.explanation: Handicaps add challenge for the stronger team, not free points.

distractors.answer: A weaker team is made to play with fewer players so that the contest stays challenging
distractors.explanation: Handicaps balance the contest fairly, not by disadvantaging the weaker team.

distractors.answer: The scoreboard is hidden so that neither team can tell who is winning the match
distractors.explanation: Handicaps balance scoring; they do not hide the score.

toLevel3.question: Why are modifications central to fair play?
toLevel3.correct: Standard rules and equipment may not suit everyone, so modifications keep play fair

distractors.answer: Standard rules already suit everyone equally, so modifications are never really needed
distractors.explanation: Standard rules may not suit everyone, which is why modifications help.

distractors.answer: Modifications mainly speed up the game rather than making the play fairer for all
distractors.explanation: Modifications are used to keep play fair and inclusive.

distractors.answer: Fair play depends only on the referee, so the rules and equipment do not matter
distractors.explanation: Equipment and rules strongly affect fairness, not only the referee.

toLevel3.question: Why does modified equipment support inclusion?
toLevel3.correct: Lighter balls, smaller bats, or larger goals let more people join in successfully
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Modified equipment lets more join in.

distractors.answer: Heavier balls and smaller goals raise the challenge so that fewer people can join in
distractors.explanation: Modified equipment is easier, helping more people join in.

distractors.answer: Changing the equipment affects only safety and has no effect on who can join in
distractors.explanation: Modified equipment also affects who can participate successfully.

distractors.answer: Modified equipment mainly benefits elite players rather than beginners or newcomers
distractors.explanation: Modified equipment helps newcomers and beginners take part.

toLevel3.question: Why do rule modifications shape inclusion?
toLevel3.correct: Rule changes can make games safer, slower, or simpler so more people can play

distractors.answer: Rule changes always make games faster and harder so that only experts can keep up
distractors.explanation: Rule modifications can simplify or slow games to include more players.

distractors.answer: Rule changes affect only the scoring and never how safe or simple a game is
distractors.explanation: Rule changes can affect safety and simplicity, not only scoring.

distractors.answer: Rule changes are decided by tradition alone and cannot be used for inclusion
distractors.explanation: Rule changes are a key tool for inclusion.

toLevel3.question: Why do scoring modifications keep games fair?
toLevel3.correct: They balance teams of different ability so the result reflects effort, not just skill

distractors.answer: They make sure the more skilful team always wins by a comfortable margin each time
distractors.explanation: Scoring modifications balance the contest rather than ensuring the skilful win.

distractors.answer: They remove the score completely so that effort and skill no longer matter at all
distractors.explanation: Scoring is balanced, not removed.

distractors.answer: They reward only raw skill so the most talented team is certain to come out ahead
distractors.explanation: Scoring modifications let effort count, not just skill.

toLevel3.question: Why is mixed-ability play powerful in inclusion?
toLevel3.correct: Playing alongside others builds skill, friendship, and respect across abilities

distractors.answer: Playing alongside others mainly creates rivalry that pushes different abilities apart
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability play builds respect and connection, not division.

distractors.answer: Playing alongside others helps only the most skilful while holding everyone else back
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability play benefits players across abilities.

distractors.answer: Playing alongside others improves fitness but builds no friendship or mutual respect
distractors.explanation: Mixed-ability play builds friendship and respect too.

toLevel3.question: Why is adapted sport like wheelchair basketball important?
toLevel3.correct: It shows top-level competition with modifications, making sport open to more people

distractors.answer: It shows that high-level sport is possible only without any modifications at all
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport shows high-level competition with modifications.

distractors.answer: It proves that modified sport can never reach a genuinely competitive standard
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport reaches elite competitive standards.

distractors.answer: It keeps elite sport closed to all but a small group of able-bodied athletes
distractors.explanation: Adapted sport opens elite competition to more people.

toLevel3.question: Why are Paralympic Games globally significant?
toLevel3.correct: They showcase adapted sport at the highest level for athletes with disabilities

distractors.answer: They showcase only able-bodied athletes competing under completely standard rules
distractors.explanation: The Paralympics showcase athletes with disabilities under adapted rules.

distractors.answer: They are small local events with little global profile or audience interest
distractors.explanation: The Paralympics are a globally significant event.

distractors.answer: They prove that adapted sport cannot be played at any serious competitive level
distractors.explanation: The Paralympics show adapted sport at the highest level.

toLevel3.question: Why does Auslan use in sport matter for deaf athletes?
toLevel3.correct: Signed instructions and signals allow full participation in team play

distractors.answer: Signed instructions replace the rules so that deaf athletes follow a separate game
distractors.explanation: Signing supports communication within the same game, not a separate one.

distractors.answer: Signed instructions help only the coach and leave players unable to take part
distractors.explanation: Signing enables the players' own full participation.

distractors.answer: Signed instructions are useful in training but never during an actual match
distractors.explanation: Signing supports participation during matches too.

toLevel3.question: Why do bench rotations matter in inclusive games?
toLevel3.correct: They make sure all players get game time, not just the strongest

distractors.answer: They make sure the strongest players stay on the field for the whole game
distractors.explanation: Rotation shares game time rather than favouring the strongest.

distractors.answer: They are used mainly to slow the game down rather than to share game time
distractors.explanation: Rotation is about fair game time, not pace.

distractors.answer: They give extra game time only to players who are already the most skilled
distractors.explanation: Rotation shares time with all players, not only the skilled.

toLevel3.question: Why are goal handicaps used in mixed-ability games?
toLevel3.correct: They balance teams of different ability so games stay engaging for both sides

distractors.answer: They guarantee that the stronger team wins easily so the contest is never close
distractors.explanation: Handicaps keep games balanced and engaging, not one-sided.

distractors.answer: They remove competition entirely so that neither side is trying to win the game
distractors.explanation: Handicaps balance competition rather than removing it.

distractors.answer: They reward skill alone so the weaker team has no real chance of staying close
distractors.explanation: Handicaps give the weaker team a fair chance.

toLevel3.question: Why can First Nations games like Kolap or Marngrook be adapted?
toLevel3.correct: Modifications open these games to wider participation while honouring their tradition
toLevel3.correctExplanation: First Nations games can be adapted.

distractors.answer: Modifications strip out the cultural tradition so that only the modern rules remain
distractors.explanation: Respectful modification honours the tradition rather than removing it.

distractors.answer: Modifications make these games harder so that fewer people are able to take part
distractors.explanation: Modifications widen participation rather than narrowing it.

distractors.answer: Modifications change only the names of the games rather than how they are played
distractors.explanation: Modifications adjust play while honouring the tradition.

toLevel3.question: Why is consulting players part of fair modification?
toLevel3.correct: Players know what works for them, and consultation builds inclusive, agreed rules

distractors.answer: Players rarely understand their own needs, so consultation usually wastes valuable time
distractors.explanation: Players' input is valuable and central to fair modification.

distractors.answer: Consultation matters only for coaches, since players have little useful to contribute
distractors.explanation: Players have important input into what works for them.

distractors.answer: Agreed rules come from tradition alone, so asking players changes nothing at all
distractors.explanation: Consulting players shapes inclusive, agreed rules.
